name: request_over_budget
summary: The request body outgrew the capture budget, so the turn was shed before any ingest work.
trigger: Accumulating another request-body chunk would have pushed the capture buffer past requestCaptureBudget, the largest request the ingest POST can carry (ingest's body limit minus the envelope reserve).
grounding: Transport: the budget is derived from one deployment's ingest body limit and envelope reserve — a property of where the bytes are being sent, not of what a turn is. A request this large can never land at that ingest, so buffering it fully and letting the POST fail would spend memory to reach the same loss; capture stops instead, while every chunk is still acked and forwarding is untouched. An implementation that writes turns synchronously, or whose sink has no body limit, can never emit it.
not_expressible: The budget trip is a comparison against accumulated runtime state, not a property of data a case can carry.
notes: Like sem_full, the turn was fine and the capture path chose to shed it — here because the loss was already certain at ingest's body limit. Distinct from ingest_reject, which is the receiver refusing bytes that were actually sent.
